description: A clock distributor that walks a 64 step sequence of letters and sends each clock pulse to whichever of thirteen outputs the current letter names

params.text: Sets how often a step rewrites the sequence around it by the rule its own letter names, 0 to 100 per cent of clocks
Sets where in the module's fixed random table the sequence is read from, 0 to 64, which changes every letter at once
Sets how often a step replaces its own letter with a fresh random one, 0 to 100 per cent of clocks

inputs.text: Advances the sequence one step on each rising edge above 2V, and sets how many polyphonic channels the outputs carry
Holds the sequence at its first step while it reads above 2V; every channel of a cable here is summed first, so any channel high resets

outputs.text: 10V while the current letter is the first of the two marked on it and the clock is high, 10V while the letter is the second and the clock is low, and 0V otherwise

notes: nothing comes out until a clock is patched to CLK: the outputs take their channel count from that cable and carry none without it
one of the twenty-seven letters is a blank, and on a step carrying it no output goes high at all
the display shows the next eight letters and the three lamps mark a rewrite, the clock and a randomisation; both are drawn rather than built from controls, so no click reaches them
on a polyphonic clock each channel hands its letter on to the next channel on that channel's own rising edge, so the channels run as an arpeggio down the cable

inputs.0:
high above 2V · stepped · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1:
high above 2V · stepped · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
